items.headline: MAS tightens policy for a second straight quarter as inflation risks climb
items.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore slightly raised the rate of appreciation of the S$NEER band on 27 July, its second straight quarterly tightening, and said core inflation should stay elevated into early 2027 as Middle East tensions lift oil prices. Most analysts polled had expected no change.

items.headline: HarbourFront Centre closes for redevelopment into a 33-storey tower by 2031
items.summary: HarbourFront Centre ceased operations on 27 July after a final trading day. The 14-storey retail-and-ferry complex will be demolished and rebuilt as a 33-storey mixed-use development with 26 floors of Grade A offices and a 13,000 sqm elevated park, targeted to reopen in the first half of 2031.

items.headline: Car driver, 30, dies in early-morning CTE crash with a lorry
items.summary: A 30-year-old man driving a BMW died at the scene of a collision with a lorry on the CTE towards the SLE at about 4.45am on 27 July. A 37-year-old lorry driver, his 38-year-old passenger and a 24-year-old road worker were taken conscious to Tan Tock Seng Hospital; police investigations are ongoing.

items.headline: Woman, 46, arrested after a fire at a Sembawang HDB flat
items.summary: A 46-year-old woman was taken to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation after a fire broke out at a Sembawang HDB flat, and was arrested for mischief by fire, the police said.

items.headline: RBI dollar sales lift the rupee to its biggest gain in over a month
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India intervened in the currency market on 27 July, selling dollars as the rupee traded near 96.15 and driving it up as much as 0.8% to about 95.78 — its largest single-day gain since mid-June and a sharp reversal from recent record lows.

items.headline: Monsoon floods across India's northeast kill at least 40 and affect 650,000
items.summary: Weeks of monsoon rain have flooded Assam and neighbouring northeastern states, killing at least 40 people with dozens missing. More than 650,000 have been affected across 11 districts, and the army has been deployed for rescues in Manipur.

items.headline: Infosys cuts its revenue forecast and names a new chief executive
items.summary: Infosys trimmed the top end of its annual sales forecast on 23 July and named a new chief executive to steer it through a prolonged slowdown in technology spending, underscoring weak demand across India's IT-services sector.

items.headline: Update: Youth protesters widen demands to Modi and Shah as opposition stalls Parliament
items.summary: After forcing the education minister's resignation, India's Gen Z 'Cockroach' movement escalated its demands this week to include the resignations of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah, while opposition MPs disrupted the monsoon session for a full week.

items.headline: Burnham says the UK must get serious about cutting its welfare bill
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham signalled the government will make benefits harder to claim, floating payments conditional on accepting work or training as it confronts a soaring welfare bill. Some Labour backbenchers warned against what they called punitive cuts.

items.headline: UK youth unemployment climbs to 16.4% as Burnham readies a skills plan
items.summary: Youth unemployment in Britain has reached a decade-plus high of 16.4%, and Burnham is due to set out education and further-training proposals this week that he argues — rather than benefit cuts — are the key to bringing young people back to work.

items.headline: UK inflation pressures ease as the Bank of England prepares to hold rates
items.summary: Domestically generated price pressures are finally cooling for the Bank of England, whose policymakers meet this week. Markets expect rates held at 3.75%, with consumer price inflation running at about 2.8%.

items.headline: A fourth summer heatwave brings amber alerts and a London hosepipe ban
items.summary: Amber heat-health alerts are in force as a fourth heatwave pushes south-east England toward 35C midweek, after Thames Water imposed a hosepipe ban across the London area following a run of record-breaking heatwaves.

items.headline: Israel's security cabinet approves an international stabilisation force for Gaza
items.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security cabinet approved the legal framework for a multinational International Stabilisation Force under the US-brokered ceasefire plan, clearing about 200 personnel from countries including Uganda and Morocco to deploy in areas outside Israeli control, over far-right objections.

items.headline: Wildfires force more than 300,000 to flee across France and Spain
items.summary: A third consecutive heatwave has fuelled wildfires around Bordeaux and Madrid, burning roughly 10,000 hectares in the Madrid region. Spain declared a national emergency and France appealed for international help as President Macron convened a crisis meeting.

items.headline: Pakistan's monsoon death toll passes 100 as floods batter Punjab and KP
items.summary: Rain-related incidents since late June have killed at least 107 people and injured 344 across Pakistan, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab worst hit. Fresh flood warnings prompted evacuations by boat in Muridke district.

items.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Russia's Belgorod, wounding a dozen overnight
items.summary: An overnight drone barrage on 26-27 July hit Belgorod, killing two people and wounding around 17 across Belgorod and the Rostov region, according to Russian officials, setting a residential block and cars ablaze and triggering an emergency power outage.

items.headline: Trump sets 50% tariffs on Canada and Brazil before an August 1 deadline
items.summary: President Trump moved to impose additional 50% tariffs on billions of dollars of Canadian goods and singled out Brazil with a 50% duty tied to Bolsonaro's prosecution, prompting Brazil's President Lula to threaten retaliation as an 1 August tariff deadline approaches.

items.headline: Nvidia in talks to backstop $250 billion of financing for an OpenAI data centre
items.summary: Nvidia is discussing guaranteeing roughly $250 billion in financing to help OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt, roughly $500 billion data-centre campus being developed by SoftBank's SB Energy — a move that would help OpenAI raise debt despite lacking an investment-grade credit rating.

items.headline: China's Moonshot releases Kimi K3 open weights, its largest model yet
items.summary: Moonshot AI published the downloadable weights for Kimi K3, a roughly 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model it says rivals leading US systems at a fraction of the cost, sharpening US concern over competitive Chinese open models.

items.headline: Google's AI Overviews now appear in about 43% of searches, new data shows
items.summary: New data indicates Google's AI-generated Overviews surface in roughly 43% of searches, accelerating the shift to AI answers and deepening publisher complaints that AI citations rarely drive referral clicks.

items.headline: Robotics startup Enigma raises $71 million to simplify human-robot control
items.summary: Enigma, less than a year old, raised a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, and is opening more than 100 of its AI robots in Israel and California to public online interaction.

items.headline: Dow rises as oil retreats while the S&P 500 holds flat and the Nasdaq slips
items.summary: The Dow rose 0.51% to about 52,210 on 27 July as falling oil lifted sentiment, while the S&P 500 was essentially flat at about 7,413 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.18% on semiconductor weakness, ahead of Big Tech earnings and the Federal Reserve's rate decision.

items.headline: Argenx agrees to buy Forte Biosciences for about $2.2 billion
items.summary: Belgian biotech Argenx agreed to acquire Forte Biosciences for roughly $2.2 billion in cash, or $77 a share — an 86% premium — to add an antibody being developed for vitiligo and celiac disease, with the all-cash deal expected to close in the third quarter.

items.headline: Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern revise their bid for a record US rail merger
items.summary: The two railroads filed a revised merger application on 27 July with new customer commitments, including enhanced oversight and temporary alternate rail service during any disruptions, in a push to complete what would be the industry's biggest-ever combination.

items.headline: EQT raises its takeover offer for Australia's Perpetual to about $1.8 billion
items.summary: Private-equity firm EQT lifted its bid for Australian wealth manager Perpetual to around $1.8 billion, sweetening terms as it pursues the asset manager.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen's charge to second lifts Red Bull as F1 breaks for summer
items.summary: Max Verstappen recovered from a qualifying spin to finish second behind race winner Lando Norris at the Hungarian Grand Prix and was voted Driver of the Day. He enters the summer break seventh on 91 points, 113 behind leader Kimi Antonelli, with his home Dutch GP at Zandvoort (21-23 Aug) up next.

items.headline: 🏏 Trent Rockets chase down London Spirit for a thrilling Hundred win
items.summary: Trent Rockets chased 159 for 9 — the highest chase at Trent Bridge in the Hundred — to beat London Spirit by four wickets with two balls to spare on 26 July, Ben Duckett's 47-ball 75 anchoring the win before Craig Overton hit the winning runs off his brother Jamie.

items.headline: 🏏 West Indies edge ahead of Pakistan in a tight Tarouba Test
items.summary: West Indies made 311 (Shai Hope 89 not out, Kavem Hodge 84) and dismissed Pakistan for 282 in the first Test at Tarouba, then slipped to 15 for 2 in their second innings for a lead of 44, leaving the match finely poised on day three of five.

items.headline: 🎾 De Minaur and Tsitsipas headline as the DC Open gets under way
items.summary: The Mubadala Citi DC Open began on 27 July in Washington, with defending champion Alex de Minaur drawn against Stefanos Tsitsipas in a standout first-round tie; Jessica Pegula, Naomi Osaka and Madison Keys lead the WTA 500 field.

items.headline: Hubble finds star formation across the Andromeda galaxy is winding down
items.summary: Combining two large Hubble surveys that mapped two-thirds of Andromeda's disk, astronomers found star formation has declined over the past 500 million years, with an especially steep drop in the last 40 million, NASA reported.

items.headline: Earlier prescribed burns spared thousands of giant sequoias from megafires
items.summary: A Nature Communications study of 26,403 giant sequoias across 19 groves found recent megafires killed about 30% of them, but prescribed burns within the prior decade cut a tree's odds of dying by 77%, sparing nearly 2,000 giants.

items.headline: Gut-to-brain vagus nerve signals help the brain form memories, study finds
items.summary: USC researchers report in Nature Communications that nutrient intake triggers vagus-nerve-mediated acetylcholine release in the hippocampus to support memory formation in rats — a response abolished by severing the nerve or by an early-life Western diet.

items.headline: Scientists turn telecom fibre into dense sensors to speed earthquake alerts
items.summary: A new Nature Communications study shows how P-wave strain measured on borehole strainmeters and Distributed Acoustic Sensing — repurposing ordinary fibre-optic cables as dense arrays — can rapidly classify an earthquake's magnitude, a step toward cheaper early-warning coverage.

fun_fact.headline: Alaska is the most northern, western, and eastern US state at once
fun_fact.body: Alaska is simultaneously the most northern, western, and eastern state in the US; its Aleutian Islands cross the 180th meridian into the Eastern Hemisphere.

puzzle.title: Who Broke the Vase?
puzzle.body: One of four children broke a vase; each makes one statement and exactly one statement is true. Who did it?
puzzle.approach: Two statements are logical opposites, so exactly one of that pair is true.

word_puzzle.title: Less Is More
word_puzzle.body: Turn LESS into MORE, one letter per step, four steps.
word_puzzle.approach: Change one letter at a time; every rung a real word.
